This application coming on for hearing this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER I.A. No.7924/2024, application for seeking exemption for filing affidavit.
For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed.

This second bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.178 of 2023 registered at Police Station Mayapur, District Shivpuri (M.P.), for offence punishable under Sections 376 of IPC, Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 3(1)(w)(i) and 3(2)(v)
of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

sentences.text:
Thereafter, victim (PW-1)
and her father (PW-2) have been examined before the learned trial Court.
As per the prosecution case, vicitim aged around 16 years reported to Police Station Mayapur that on 22.08.2023 in the evening, she went to answer the nature call.
Accused Pushpendra Lodhi followed her and finding her alone committed rape on her.
She complained to her parents and brother-in-law and thereafter came to report.

On such allegations, Police Station Mayapur, District Shivpuri registered FIR at Crime No.178 of 2023 for offence punishable under Sections 376 of IPC,
Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 3(1)(w)(i) and 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Victim was forwarded for medico legal examination.
Her statement was recorded.
The sample of victim and accused Pushpendra Lodhi forwarded to DNA examination.
DNA examination suggested sexual intercourse between victim and applicant.
Applicant was arrested on 25.08.2023.
He is in custody ever since.

On completion of investigation,
Final Report was submitted on 21.09.2023.
The trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter under the pressure of family members of the victim.
It is a case of consensual relationship between two young persons.
Learned counsel referring to the statements of PW-1 and PW-2 submits that both of them have not supported the prosecution.
Victim has stated that she got married two years back.
She was aged around 19 years at the time of marriage.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is Agriculturist by profession and is aged around 19 years.
There is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence.
Trial would take time to complete.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case regard being had to the young age of the applicant, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant Pushpendra Lodhi shall be released on bail in relation to Crime No.178 of 2023 registered at Police Station Mayapur, District Shivpuri (M.P.), for offence punishable under Sections 376 of IPC, Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 3(1)(w)(i) and 3(2)(v)
of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, for compliance with the following conditions, :
